name: Gadādhara Bhaṭṭa
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Raṅgadevī**, the seventh of Śrī Rādhā's eight principal sakhīs, twin sister of Sudevī.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 165

> raṅgadevī purā yāsīd adya bhaṭṭo gadādharaḥ
> anantācārya-gosvāmī yā sudevī purā vraje

«The vraja-gopī Raṅgadevī appeared as Gadādhara Bhaṭṭa, and the vraja-gopī Sudevī appeared as Ananta Ācārya Gosvāmī.»

## Raṅgadevī in the books

- **Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā** (Bṛhad-bhāga 94–95): her complexion resembles the colour of lotus-pollen and her clothes have the colour of the somewhat reddish javā flower; she is seven days younger than Śrī Rādhā and her qualities resemble Campakalatā's. «Śrī Raṅgadevī's father is Raṅgasāra and her mother is Karuṇā. Her husband, whose name is Vakrekṣaṇa, is the younger brother of Bhairava.» Her twin sister Sudevī is so like her that she is sometimes taken for her (96).

## Other opinions

- The Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna gives this identity to a Gadādhara Bhaṭṭa of Hanumānpur in Tailaṅga-deśa, and names the disciple of Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa in a second entry: perhaps two persons. Whisper (15-11-2026): this record is the Raṅgadevī of the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā.

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 165; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Bṛhad-bhāga 79, 94–96.
